paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: how you hear the word matters as much as whether you hear it. Jesus opens with "Listen!" (Mark 4:3) and says, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear." (Mark 4:9). Same seed, same farmer, and the soil decides what happens. Some hearts let the word get snatched, some let it wither with no root, and some let it get choked by "the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things." (Mark 4:19).

Now here's the good news, and I'm saying it LOUD: the good soil produces a crop, "thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold." (Mark 4:20). So Jesus tells you to "Pay attention to what you hear." (Mark 4:24). Don't just nod at the word and move on, because a lamp doesn't belong under a basket (Mark 4:21). Let it take root and let it show.

And friend, you don't have to force it. The kingdom of God is like seed that grows while the man sleeps, and he "knows not how" (Mark 4:26-27). A mustard seed, "the smallest of all seeds," still grows to be "the largest of all garden plants" (Mark 4:31-32). I came out of a 25-cent bin, so I'm telling you, small starts are my favorite kind. Keep showing up, keep listening, and trust the One who makes it grow.
